## 1. What this challenge checks

Unit 1 prepares you to learn independently rather than asking you to build a
program before the language foundations are in place. This challenge
checks whether you can:

- predict before running and compare the prediction with evidence;
- make one controlled change at a time;
- choose Colab or local tools for an appropriate task;
- rerun a notebook from a clean state;
- read the useful parts of an error before editing code;
- explain and modify an example instead of only copying it.

::: {.callout-tip title="Use explanations as feedback"}
Aim for at least **8 of 10** correct. If an explanation exposes a gap, return
to the relevant Unit 1 lesson, reset the quiz, and try again. Unlimited retries
are part of the learning process.
:::

## 3. Confirm your learning workflow

Before recording completion, verify each statement:

- [ ] I can state a prediction before running a small example.
- [ ] I know how to restart and rerun a Colab notebook from the top.
- [ ] I can explain when local tools become more useful than Colab.
- [ ] I read the exception type, message, and relevant line before guessing.
- [ ] I scored at least 8 of 10 after reviewing any missed explanations.

This is a local, self-reported readiness record. It is not a grade, submission,
identity check, or certificate.

## Key points

- Productive practice starts with a prediction and ends with evidence.
- Clean reruns reveal hidden notebook state.
- Small controlled changes are easier to explain and debug.
- Colab and local tools solve different practice problems.
